541.e: Ans. D. Half hand method Methods of delivery of aftercoming head are Burns - Marshall method ForcePs delivery Malar flexion and shoulder traction (modified Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit technique)

541.q: A 22-year-old pregnant woman presents with dysuria and increased frequency. A urinary tract infection is diagnosed. What is the most appropriate step?
o: Treatment if the c-reactive protein(CRP) is high
Treatment if the erythrocyte sedimentation rate(ESR) is high
541.e: Infections in pregnancy should be treated, as 25% of patients will develop acute pyelonephritis. Nitrofurantoin, cephalosporins and beta lactams are safe in pregnancy. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21 st ed, Ch: 135, Pg: 1077.

542.q: A female at 37 weeks of gestation has mild labour pains for 10 hours and cervix is persistently 1 cm dilated but non effaced. What will be the next appropriate management?
542.e: The patient in the question has been having mild labor pains for 10 hours with no change in cervical dilatation and effacement. But again the question does not specify whether she is having regular uterine contractions or not. False labor can be differentiated from latent phase of labor by therapeutic rest i.eThe patient is sedated with morphine. So the correct option is Sedate and Wait. As far as augmentation with oxytocin is concerned - it is done only in those patients who even after therapeutic rest continue to be in prolonged latent phase (once the diagnosis of lack of progress of latent phase is confirmed following therapeutic rest.) Amniotomy is not useful and should be avoided in patients in prolonged latent phase. Also, there is no indication of cesarean section in this case. Reference : Fernando Arias 3/e, pg 376

542.q: All of the following drugs are effective for cervical ripening during pregnancy except:
542.e: Ripening of the cervix is changing the cervical matrix from sol to gel state by dissolving the collagen bundles. Ultimately the cervix becomes soft. Techniques for cervical ripening: Pharmacological: Dinoprostone gel (PGE 2 ) - it is the gold standard for cervical ripening Misoprostol (PGE1) tablet - vaginal or oral Steroid receptor antagonist Mifepristone Oxytocin Non pharmacological: Stripping the membrane Mechanical dilators: Osmotic dilators Balloon catheter/Transcervical catheter placed through internal os Extra-amniotic saline infusion Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 524; Fernando Arias 3/e, pg 284-286; Williams Obs. 24/e, pg 525

o: To stop excess bleeding from uterus
542.e: Ans, C. To stop excess bleeding from uterus Methergin (methyl-ergo-novine) is a semisynthetic ergot derivative derived from lysergic acid. Indications Prophylactic:- Active management of 3rd stage of labour to prevent excess bleeding following delivery. Therapeutic:- To stop atonic uterine bleeding.

543.q: Which of the following structures is attached at cervicovaginal junction
543.e: Pelvic cellular tissue around the vaginalvault, supravaginal part of the cervix and into the layers of the broad ligament is called parametrium. Condensation occurs especially near the cervicovaginal junction to form ligaments which extend from the viscera to the pelvic walls on either side. These are Mackenrodt’s ligaments/ cardinal ligament, uterosacral ligaments and vesicocervical ligaments (fascia). All these constitute important supports of the uterus to keep it in position. Reference: DC Dutta textbook of obstetrics, 8th edition; chapter 1

543.q: All are seen with scar dehiscence, except:
543.e: All are seen with scar dehiscence, except (A) Maternal bradycardia. Maternal bradycardia is not typically associated with scar dehiscence; the other options, such as fetal bradycardia, vaginal bleeding, and hematuria, can occur. Uterine rupture typically is classified as either complete (all layers of the uterine wall separated) or incomplete (uterine muscle separated but visceral peritoneum is intact). Incomplete rupture is commonly referred to as scar dehiscence. Scar dehiscence is an intraoperative finding always. The greatest risk factor for either complete or incomplete uterine rupture is prior cesarean delivery. "The most common sign of uterine rupture is a non-reassuring fetal heart rate pattern with variable deceleration evolving into late decelerations, bradycardia and undetectable fetal heart rate pattern". Reference: John Hopkins Manual of Obs. and Gynae 4/e, p 86

543.q: The only disadvantage of active management of IIIrd stage of labor is:
543.e: In this method the placenta separation is actively facilitated and powerful uterine contractions are initiated to reduce the incidence of third stage complications (like PPH) Duration is reduced to 5 mins so less bleeding, less chances of PPH and less maternal mortality Active management of labor includes Administration of a uterotonic soon after birth of baby Delayed cord clamping Delivery of placenta by controlled cord traction Uterine message The only drawback of active management of 3rd stage of labor is , since uterotonic agent is given at the delivery of shoulder before the delivery placenta, it can lead to increased chances of Retained placenta. Reference : Williams 24/e, pg 513

544.q: Which is responsible for fetal heart rate acceleration?
544.e: Explanation: Fetal heart rate acceleration is primarily mediated by the autonomic nervous system. Sympathetic stimulation (via noradrenaline) increases heart rate, especially during fetal movement or external stimuli. Parasympathetic (vagal) tone slows heart rate ; transient withdrawal of vagal activity can also cause accelerations. Fetal heart rate accelerations are considered a sign of fetal well-being and neurological integrity. Neither baroreceptors nor chemoreceptors play a primary role in causing accelerations, though they are involved in other fetal heart rate responses (Option A, B, D ruled out). Clinical episodes of acceleration often occur with fetal activity or stimulation, confirming autonomic system involvement. Reference: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8061630/ , http://www.perinatology.com/Fetal%20Monitoring/Intrapartum%20Monitoring.htm

544.q: Which of the following is false for vaginal anatomy in non pregnant state
o: Anterior and posterior walls are opposed together
It looks H shaped on sagittal section
Length of posterior wall is more than length of anterior wall
544.e: Vagina has got an anterior, a posterior and two lateral walls. The anterior and posterior walls are opposed together but the lateral walls are comparatively stiffer especially at its middle, as such, it looks “H” shaped on the transverse section. The length of the anterior wall is about 7 cm and that of the posterior wall is about 9 cm. Reference: DC Dutta textbook of obstetrics, 8th edition; chapter 1

544.q: A 39-year-old female with G6P3L3A2 came to OPD having full term pregnancy with previous 3 LSCS. She is diagnosed case of PAS. What will not be mentioned in the consent?
o: Chances of bowel injury due to PAS
Chances of bladder injury due to PAS
Chances of hysterectomy due to PAS
544.e: Placenta Accreta Spectrum(PAS) disorder has disastrous outcome for both mother and fetus. Chances of bowel injury are very rare It includes: Placenta A ccreta: Placenta A dherent to myometrium Placenta I ncreta: Placenta I nvading myometrium Placenta P ercreta: Placenta P erforating through myometrium Cause: Due to absence of Nitabuch's layer It should be terminated at tertiary care center. Complication of surgery for PAS includes: Long operative time Blood and blood product transfusion(Option D) Surgical complications like bladder injury(Option B) ICU admission Increased length of stay Management: Caesarean Hysterectomy(Option C)

545.q: Screening by using maternal serum alpha fetoproteins helps to detect all of the following except:
545.e: Some conditions associated with abnormal maternal serum alpha fetoprotein concentration. Elevated levels Error in dates Multifetal pregnancy Severe oligohydramnios Neural tube defects Pilonidal cysts Esophageal or intestinal obstruction (and atresia) Liver necrosis Cystic hygroma Sacrococcygeal teratoma Fetal death Abdominal wall defects: omphalocele gastroschisis Urinary obstruction Renal anomalies: polycystic kidney absent kidneys Congenital nephrosis Osteogenesis imperfecta Congenital skin defects Cloacal exstrophy Chorioangioma of placenta Low birth weight Placental abruption Placenta accreta Preeclampsia Improper adjustment for low maternal weight Maternal hepatoma or teratoma Low level G: G estational trophoblastic diseases O 2 : O verestimated gestational age, overweight mother A: Spontaneous a bortion T: T risomy (21 or 18) Reference: Williams Obs. 24/e, p 287

545.q: Obstetric shock Index (OSI) is calculated by:
o: Heart rate divided by Mean arterial pressure
Heart rate divided by Diastolic blood pressure
Heart rate divided by Systolic blood pressure
Heart rate divided by Pulmonary arterial pressure
545.e: Shock index (SI) refers to heart rate (HR) divided by systolic blood pressure (SBP). The normal value is 0.5–0.7. For obstetric shock index (OSI) normal value in pregnancy is 0.7–0.8. Increase in the pulse rate and a fall in systolic blood pressure that is seen with significant haemorrhage, results in an increase in the shock index. If it increases above 0.9–1.1, intensive resuscitation may be required. If OSI > 1 indicates massive blood obstetric haemorrhage that required blood transfusion. Reference:Arias practical guide to high risk pregnancy and delivery 4 th edition, chapter 23

545.q: A cesarean section was done in the previous pregnancy. All of the following would be indications for elective cesarean section except:
545.e: Some factors that influence a successful trial of labor in a woman with prior cesarean delivery Low risk Transverse incision prior vaginal delivery appropriate counseling sufficient personnel and equipment Favors success Teaching hospital white race spontaneous labor prior fetal malpresentation 1 or 2 prior transverse incision Nonrecurrent indication current preterm pregnancy Increase failure rate Single mother Increased maternal age Macrosomic fetus Obesity Breech Multifetal pregnancy Preeclampsia EGA > 40 weeks Low-vertical incision Unknown incision Labor induction Medical disease Multiple prior cesarean deliveries Education Short interdelivery interval Liability concerns High risk Classical or T incision Prior rupture Patient refusal Transfundal surgery Obstetrical contraindication, e.g. previa Inadequate facilities Reference : Williams 24/e, p 611

546.e: Ans, A. 14 days Menstrual regulation (lnduction/Aspiration) Aspiration of endometrial cavity within l4 days of missed period in a woman with previous normal cycle. Done as an OPD procedure. Helps to detect failed abortion, molar pregnancy or ectopic Pregnancy. Contraindicated in advanced pregnancy & in presence of local pelvic inflammation.

Laparoscopy is considered the "gold standard". While it is the most reliable aid to support the clinical diagnosis, it may not be feasible to do in all cases. It is reserved only in those cases in which differential diagnosis includes salpingitis, appendicitis or ectopic pregnancy. Nonresponding pelvic mass needs laparoscopic clarification. Hysteroscopy may also provide confirmatory evidence for salpingitis. "Fallopian tube culture can be obtained laparoscopically and recently the hysteroscopic approach has been introduced. The specimen is obtained during hysteroscopy with a cytobrush." Reference : Shaw 15th/ed pg 451; William's Gynae 1st/ed pg 74; Gynecology by Ostrzenski (Lippincott Williams 2001/ 282); Dutta Gynae 6th/ed pg 130

546.q: In which part of fallopian tube ectopic pregnancy will have longest survival:
546.e: M.C site of ectopic pregnancy – Fallopian tubes . In Fallopian Tubes – M/C sites in descending order are:Ampulla > isthmus > infundibulum > interstitium Rarest overall site of ectopic pregnancy is cervix or cesarean section scan Average period of survival of ectopic pregnancy is 8 weeks. Ectopic pregnancy survives for the longest time in its annual pregnancy. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 179; CODGT 10/e, p 267

547.q: Type of cerclage done in a non-pregnant patient with cervical incompetence?
547.e: The purpose of the Lash and Lash operation is to correct the defect in the cervical wall and restore competence to the cervix, thereby allowing gestation to proceed to term. Lash and Lash operation is a pervaginal procedure done in non pregnant females Benson Durfee is an abdominal cerclage procedure that can be done oin bothe pregnant as well as non pregnant females. Wurms cerclage is an emergency cerclage procedure done during pregnancy Still, Laparoscopic cerclage is the most preferred operative procedure in non pregnant females.

547.q: Comprehensive emergency obstetric care does not include:
547.e: Setting standards of emergency obstetrics and newborn care: Basic emergency obstetric and newborn care provided in health centres, large or small include the facilities for: Administration of antibiotics, oxytocics and anticonvulsants. Manual removal of the placenta. Removal of retained products following miscarriage or abortion. Assisted vaginal delivery preferably with vacuum extractor. Comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care, typically delivered in district hospital, includes all basic functions above, plus cesarean section, safe blood transfusion and care to sick and low birth weight newborns including resuscitation. It is recommended that for every 5,00,000 people there should be 4 facilities offering comprehensive essential obstetric care. Reference: KDT 6/e, p 251,484,488,Dutta Obs 7/e, p 288

547.q: A cross-sectional analysis across obstetrics and gynecology wards in several Indian hospitals reported an MMR of 4.21 per 1,000 live births. Based on WHO guidelines, how is maternal mortality defined?
o: Death from full-term pregnancy within 24 hr of delivery
Death during pregnancy and within 1 year after delivery
Death during pregnancy and within 6 weeks of delivery
547.e: Explanation: Maternal mortality refers to the death of a woman during pregnancy or within 6 weeks (42 days) after its termination. WHO Definition: Maternal mortality is defined as the annual number of deaths of women from causes related to or worsened by pregnancy or its management (excluding accidental or incidental causes), occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days of its end, regardless of the pregnancy's duration or location. Late Maternal Death: This refers to the death of a woman from direct or indirect obstetric causes occurring more than 42 days but less than one year after the end of pregnancy. Options A, B, and C are incorrect. Reference: https://www.who.int/data/gho/indicator-metadata-registry/imr-details/4622 https://sciencedirect.com/topics/medicine-and-dentistry/maternal-mortality

548.q: A 30-year-old female patient is admitted to the Emergency Department with dyspnea, tachycardia, confusion, and other signs of hypoxia. The following laboratory data were obtained while the patient was breathing room air. PaO2 = 67 mmHg PaCO2 = 60 mmHg pH = 7.27 [HCO3-] = 26 mEq/L [Hb] = 15 g% SaO2 = 90% PvO2 = 30 mmHg SvO2 = 55% VO2 = 350 mL/min CaO2-CvO2 = 7 mL O2/100 mL Which of the following is the most appropriate classification of the patient's hypoxia?
548.e: Alveolar hypoventilation (as evidenced by the higher than normal value of Paco2) is a type of hypoxic hypoxia or hypoxemia (as evidenced by the decreased PaO2). Anemic hypoxia is characterized by a decreased concentration of hemoglobin (anemia) or a reduction in the saturation of hemoglobin with oxygen (SaO2) expected for a given Pao2, as would occur in carbon monoxide poisoning or methemoglobinemia. Stagnant hypoxia is characterized by a decreased cardiac output; in this patient, cardiac output, calculated as (VO2/CaO2 - CvO2), is 5 L/min, which is normal. In histotoxic hypoxia, oxygen extraction is impaired, and thus CaO2 - CvO2 would be less than normal and Svo2 would be greater than normal. Reference: Ganong, pp 683-691. Levitzky, pp 180-183.

548.q: Treatment of genuine stress incontinence are all except:
548.e: Pelvic floor exercises Sling operation Colposuspension (Burch) is all done for management of SUI. As far as anterior colporrhaphy is concerned - Kelly’s application is anterior colporrhaphy along with bladder neck repair, so I have included it in the correct option also. Reference: Shaw 14 th /ed p 174; Dutta gynae 5 th /ed p 387-9

548.q: Regimen used for expectant management of placenta previa is:
548.e: Expectant treatment had been advocated by Mcafee and Johnson, in an attempt to improve the fetal salvage without increasing undue maternal hazards. The aim is to continue pregnancy for fetal maturity without compromising the maternal health. Reference:-D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 19

549.q: Riskofuterine rupture in case ofuterine scar. 1317. Methergin is given for prophylaxis of ?
549.e: Ans, A. Anaemia Methergin (methyl-ergo-novine) is a semisynthetic ergot derivative derived from lysergic acid. Indications

549.q: Which of the following arteries is not ligated during stepwise devascularization for PPH?
549.e: Stepwise pelvic devascularization Uterine artery Tubal branch of ovarian artery (utero-ovarian artery) Anterior branch of internal iliac artery Reference:D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

549.q: A G2P1 had an uneventful vaginal delivery of a 3.4 kg baby girl. Placenta was completely expulsed soon after delivery. After delivery of placenta there was excessive vaginal bleeding uterus was hard and contracted. Most likely cause of bleeding would be:
549.e: Cervical tear is the commonest cause of traumatic postpartum haemorrhage. Clinical feature: Excessive vaginal bleeding immediately following delivery in presence of a hard and contracted uterus. Repair should be done under general anesthesia, in lithotomy position with a good light. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 29

550.q: Which of the following statements is true about the fetal fibronectin (fFN) test?
o: In this test fFN is measured from maternal serum
Positive test in first trimester increases risk of abortion
Negative test means delivery will not occur in next 7 days
550.e: Fibronectin is a glycoprotein that binds the fetal membranes to the decidua. Normally it is found in the cervicovaginal discharge before 22 weeks and again after 37 weeks of pregnancy. Presence of fibronectin in the cervicovaginal discharge between 24 weeks and 34 weeks is a predictor of preterm labor. When the test is negative it reassures that delivery will not occur within the next 7 days . Reference : D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

550.q: Which of the following is not a contraindication to tocolysis:
550.e: Contraindications to tocolysis Intrauterine fetal demise Lethal fetal anomaly Nonreassuring fetal status Severe preeclampsia or eclampsia Maternal bleeding with hemodynamic instability Chorioamnionitis Preterm prelabor rupture of membranes Reference : laxmi sheshadri principles of obstetric, 1 st edition, chapter-35

550.q: Pain in early labor is limited to dermatomes:
550.e: In the early stages of labour pain is mainly uterine in origin because of painful uterine contraction "The pain of uterine contractions is distributed along the cutaneous nerve distribution of T 10 to L 1 In later stages pain is due to dilatation of the cervix. "The pain of cervical dilatation and stretching is referred to the back through sacral plexus." Reference : Dutta Obs 7/e, pg 117

551.q: How does a hydatidiform mole occur?
o: Hyperplastic proliferation of trophoblast within the uterine wall
551.e: Hydatidiform mole is a rare mass that rapidly grows within the uterus. It results from hyperplastic proliferation of trophoblast within the uterine wall. It has a high potential to become choriocarcinoma. Reference - Textbook of Langman's, 12th Edition, General Embryology Page number - 43

551.q: What malignant tumor arises from trophoblastic cells?
551.e: Choriocarcinoma is a malignant tumor that arises from trophoblastic cells that may occur following normal pregnancy, abortions, or hydatidiform mole. Reference - Textbook of Langman's, 12th Edition, General Embryology Page number - 43

551.q: Theca lutein cyst is not seen in:
551.e: Theca lutein cysts are bilateral cysts seen in ovaries associated with markedly elevated levels of hCG. Conditions of pregnancy where theca lutein cysts are seen: Molar pregnancy Diabetes D alloimmunization Multifetal gestation Chronic renal failure – decreased clearance of hCG Hyperthyroidism (hCG and TSH–anatomically similar) Reference: Williams Obs 24/e, p 50

552.q: The lab for your pregnant patient indicates microcytic anemia. Optimal treatment of normocytic or mild microcytic anemia associated with pregnancy uses which of the following?
552.e: Iron deficiency microcytic anemia is the anemia that is most commonly associated with In this condition, oral iron supplementation is indicated. Reference: Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, Fourteenth Edition By Bertram G. Katzung Pg no. 834-37

552.q: All of the following are fetal complications of prolonged pregnancy except:
552.e: Fetal complications during pregnancy—There is diminished placental function, oligohydramnios and meconium stained liquor. These lead to fetal hypoxia and fetal distress. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

552.q: Which of the following is a non-surgical method for replacement of uterine inversion?
552.e: Hydrostatic(O’Sullivan’s) method: The inverted uterus is replaced into the vagina. Warm sterile fluid (up to 5 liters) is gradually instilled into the vagina through a douche nozzle. The vaginal orifice is blocked by the operator's palms supplemented by labial apposition around the palm by an assistant. Alternatively, a silicon cup (vacuum extraction cup) is placed into the vagina. The douche can be placed at a height of about 3 feet above the uterus. The water distends the vagina and the consequent increased intravaginal pressure leads to replacement of the uterus. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

553.q: A female of 36 weeks gestation presents with hypertension, blurring of vision and headache. Her blood pressure reading was 180/120 mm Hg and 174/110 mm Hg after 20 minutes. How will you manage the patient?
o: Admit the patient, start antihypertensives and continue pregnancy till term.
Admit the patient, start antihypertensives, MgSO4 and terminate the pregnancy
Admit oral antihypertensives and follow up in out-patient department
553.e: In the question, patient is presenting with Headache, Blurring of vision, B/P = 180/120 mm of Hg (later 174/110 mm of Hg) i.e. she is a case of severe pregnancy induced hypertension. First step in the management of this case would be to prevent seizures i.e. give MgSO4. Her B/P should be controlled with antihypertensive and since pregnancy is >34 weeks, therefore terminate pregnancy (which is the definitive management). Reference : Fernando Arias Practical Guide to High Risk Pregnancy and Delivery 3/e, pg 417, 420, 424

553.q: Preconceptional intake of which of the following results in decrease in incidence of neural tube defect?
553.e: "Folic acid has been shown to effectively reduce the risk of neural tube defects (NTDs). A daily 4 mg dose is recommended for patients who have had a previous pregnancy affected by neural tube defects. It should be started at least 1 month (ideally 3 months) prior to pregnancy and continued through the first 6-12 weeks of pregnancy." -COGDT 10/e, p 197 Remember: Therapeutic dose of folic acid (to be given in females with a previous history of baby with NTD) - 4 mg. Prophylactic dose of folic acid = 0.4 mg i.e., 400 mg Duration: It should be started 1 month before conception and continued till 3 months of pregnancy. Note: Women with insulin dependent diabetes mellitus and those with seizure disorders treated by valproic acid and carbamazepine are also at greater risk for NTD's and should be given therapeutic dose of folic acid i.e 4 mg. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 409; COGDT 10/e, p 197

553.q: A second gravida patient with a history of pre eclampsia comes to OPD at 5 months of amenorrhea. Which test would you like to perform for prediction of pre eclampsia in this pregnancy?
553.e: Doppler ultrasound Presence of diastolic notch between 22-24 weeks by Doppler velocimetry in the uterine artery predicts the development of preeclampsia. It is probably the best available test. Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 192

554.q: A 42-year-old man presents with headaches, excessive sweating, galactorrhoea, polyuria and polydipsia. Visual field examination reveals bitemporal hemianopia. His blood pressure is 160/110 mmHg. Blood tests: fasting glucose 150 mg/dl, prolactin 1200 mU/l (<360).What is the most probable diagnosis?
554.e: Prolactinoma: (>200) Clinical features: Amenorrhoea Galactorrhoea Infertility Compressive symptoms: B/L TEMPORAL HEMIANOPIA. DOC: CABERGOLINE - FOR ALL CASES BROMOCRIPTINE- IF PREGNANCY IS DESIRED. Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 2912

554.q: A 50-year-old male patient presents with polyuria and polydipsia of 2 months duration. He has been on a chronic medication for last 15 years. The urine is hypoosmolar. His blood sugars are normal. Which could be the drug?
554.e: Polyuria, polydipsia with large volume of hypoosmolar urine suggest the diagnosis of Diabetes insipidus. Among the following, Lithium therapy causes nephrogenic diabetes. Other drugs causing Diabetes Insipidus: Lithium, Demeclocycline, Methoxyflurane, Amphotericin B, Aminoglycosides, Cisplatin, Rifampin, Foscarnet. Lithium causes DI by entering the Collecting Duct via the ENaC, where it down regulates the Aquaporin channels. Lithium also causes Chronic Tubulointerstitial Disease. Amiloride can be used to prevent and treat Lithium induced Diabetes Insipidus. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Ch: 316, Pg: 2363.

554.q: As per IAS DP the proposed single step testing with a 75 gram oral glucose for gestational diabetes, the fasting glucose cut off is
554.e: It is recommended that an FPG( Fasting plasma glucose) value in early pregnancy ≥5.1 mmol/l (92 mg/dl) should also be classified as Gestational Diabetes Mellitus. International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups Consensus Panel; Metzger BE, Gabbe SG, Persson B, Buchanan TA, Catalano PA, Damm P, Dyer AR, Leiva Ad, Hod M, Kitzmiller JL, Lowe LP, McIntyre HD, Oats JJ, Omori Y, Schmidt MI. International association of diabetes and pregnancy study groups recommendations on the diagnosis and classification of hyperglycemia in pregnancy.

555.q: Indication of methotrexate in molar pregnancy:
555.e: Protocol for management of H. mole Prophylactic chemotherapy: Routine prophylactic chemotherapy is not advocated now at all. Earlier in the following conditions chemotherapy was given. Conditions: Initial high levels of b-hCG (> 100,000 mIU/ml) Elevation of serum hCG at 4–6 weeks or hCG values fail to come back to normal by stipulated truth (10-12 weeks). Evidence of metastasis irrespective of hCG levels. Age of patient > 35 years. Theca lutein cyst 6 cm Post evacuation hemorrhage. Drug used : Methotrexate/Actinomycin D is given for 5 days. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 200, 196; COGDT 10/e, p 890; Shaw 14/e, p 231

555.q: A pregnant female develops an embolism just after delivery. What medical management should she take?
555.e: Venous thromboembolism in pregnancy Venous thromboembolism is the leading cause of maternal deaths in developed countries. Investigations Recommended method during pregnancy: Doppler ultrasound Gold standard (in conditions other than pregnancy): Venography Though objective evidence is ideal, treatment should be started on clinical grounds, if confirmatory tests are not available. Management For postpartum venous thrombosis, treatment with i/v heparin and warfarin are started simultaneously 6-8 hours after vaginal delivery and 24 hours after cesarean section and once INR is between 2 and 3, heparin is discontinued and warfarin is continued for 6 weeks. Note: Warfarin is absolutely safe in lactation. Reference : Williams 23/e, pg 1028, 29, Table 47.6

555.q: Patients with organic heart disease in pregnancy most commonly die during:
555.e: This is another way of asking, cardiac failure occurs most commonly at what time as the M/C cause of death in pregnant females with heart disease is congestive heart failure. Reference: Dutta Obs 7/e, p 225

556.e: Anti D prophylaxis should be given after all types of abortions (threatened, medical, MTP) molar pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, delivery (+manual removal of placenta), procedures performed antenatally (Amniocentesis, Chorionic villous sampling, External cephalic version) and in cases of antepartum hemorrhage (Vaginal bleeding in this case). Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 344 "key points"; Shiela Balakrishnan, pg 369

556.q: Which type of Hb is not affected by Rh isoimmuni- sation:
556.e: The correct answer is (C): Anti Lewis. Anti Lewis antibodies are not affected by Rh isoimmunization, while Anti D, Anti C, and Anti E are all associated with Rh blood group antigens.Anti C and Anti E antibodies can also be produced in response to blood group incompatibilities, but their effects are generally less severe than those of Anti D The Lewis antigens do not cause erythroblastosis fetalis and differ from all of the other red cell antigens in that they are not synthesized in the red cell membrane but are absorbed into it." Reference: Fernando Arias 2/e, p 116

557.q: A 26-year-old woman comes with irregular vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal pain over the past 4 days. Physical examination shows a friable cervix, and cervical and adnexal tenderness. You prescribe doxycycline and a second medication. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of the most appropriate second drug used to treat this infection?
o: Binding at the D-ala-D-ala muramyl pentapeptide to prevent transglycosylation reactions
Binds to microtubules and causes mitotic arrest in metaphase
Inhibits DNA synthesis in virally infected cells
Inhibits peptidoglycan synthesis through the blockade of transpeptidation enzymes
557.e: This patient has signs of pelvic inflammatory disease, and since distinguishing diagnostic clues are not provided here, the answer should pertain to the most common causes, which include Chlamydia and gonococcal infection. Infections of the cervix may present as an erythematous, edematous, and friable cervix, but most often are without obvious signs or symptoms. Early signs and symptoms of a chlamydial infection in women tend to be mild and include pain during urination, frequent urination, and low-grade fever. Later symptoms can be more intense and include nausea, fatigue, and abnormal discharge from the vagina. Other symptoms include abdominal pain, lower back pain, irregular menstrual bleeding or spotting, and pain during sex. Reference: Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, Fourteenth Edition By Bertram G. Katzung Pg no. 816

557.q: At what gestational age should pregnancy with cholestasis of pregnancy be terminated.
557.e: Also know Management of Intrahepatic Cholestasis – Medical Management The most troublesome feature of intrahepatic cholestasis is pruritus (and pruritus is due to bile acid in blood): Pruritus can be managed temporarily with antihistamines and topical emollients Ursodeoxycholic acid (10-15 mg/kg/d in 2 divided doses) relieves pruritus decreasing in the concentration of bile acid in blood and it also improves biochemical abnormalities. In patients of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy – there is increased perinatal mortality. Hence fetal surveillance is done with biweekly NST. Conventional antepartum testing, does not predict fetal mortality as there is sudden death in choletasis due to acute hypoxia, hence delivery is recommended at 37-38 weeks. Reference : COGDT 10/e, pg 382; Williams Obs 24/e, pg 1085 Mgt of High Risk Pregnancy - S S Trivedi Manju Puri, pg 358

557.q: Earliest manifestation of end organ damage in chronic hypertension is
557.e: The earliest manifestation of end-organ damage in chronic hypertension is typically (B): Renal impairment. Chronic hypertension can lead to changes in kidney function and structure over time. These changes may be detectable through alterations in renal function tests, such as elevated serum creatinine levels or proteinuria. This early renal impairment often precedes other manifestations of end-organ damage such as hepatic, visual, or pulmonary complications Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 179

558.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding. Which of the following hormones is most commonly associated with shedding of the endometrium during menstruation?
558.e: Involution of the corpus luteum results in a decrease in progesterone and estradiol secretion. This occurs around day 24 of a 28-day menstrual cycle. The loss of hormonal support causes endometrial shedding. LH, FSH, GnRH and estrogen are not involved in this process. Estradiol is primarily responsible for endometrial proliferation during the earlier phases of menstrual cycle. Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 3035

558.q: A girl with primary amenorrhea with normal ovaries, absent internal genitalia with normal external genitalia. Probable diagnosis?
558.e: The question says that the girl has normal ovaries which rules out. Turners syndrome where streak gonads are seen Noonan's syndrome Androgen insensitivity syndrome gonads are testis. So by exclusion our answer is Mayer-Rokitansky Kuster-Hauser Syndrome. Mullerian agenesis or mayer-okintansky-Kuster-hauser syndrome is a congenital malformation characterized by a failure of the Mullerian ducts to develop, resulting in absent uterus and variable malformations of the vagina, while both ovaries are intact and functioning. Ovaries are present and function normally so secondary sexual characteristics are normal. External genitalia are also normal as testosterone is absent. Reference : Speroff 7th/ed p 420-421.

558.q: Primary amenorrhea with absent uterus, normal breasts and scanty pubic hair is seen in:
558.e: The patient is presenting with primary amenorrhea along with well developed breast and scanty pubic hair and axillary hair -leave no doubt regarding Testicular feminisation syndrome as the diagnosis, which c/k/a AIS (Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome) Reference : Novak 14 th /ed, pg no: 1037-1038

559.q: Most important structure preventing uterine prolapse is:
559.e: Supports of uterus have been discussed in detail earlier. Broad ligament (fold of peritoneum) and round ligaments are secondary supports of uterus and their role as support is doubtful. "Main support which prevents descent of the uterus is transverse cervical ligament (cardinal ligament) and its posterior extension the uterosacral ligament." Reference: Jeffcoate 7th/ed p 46

559.q: Gartner's cyst can be differentiated from cystocele by all except:
o: Presence of rugosities of overlying vaginal mucosa
559.e: Gartner’s cyst – are cysts of the remnants of Wolffian duct. M/C location = Anterolateral aspect of vagina and hence are often confused with cystocele. Features of Gartner’s cyst are: Upper three-fifths above the hymen develop from the fused uterovaginal canal of the Müllerian ducts. Rugosities of the overlying vaginal mucosa are lost. Vaginal mucosa over it becomes tense and shiny. Margins are well defined. Not reducible. No impulse on coughing Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 210.

559.q: Most common complication of purandare's sling surgery?
559.e: The M/C complication of Purandare cervicopexy is deepening of pouch of douglas leading to enterocele formation. Enterocele can be prevented after purandare sling surgery by obliterating pouch of Douglas at the time of operation called Moscowitz repair. Reference : J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1 st edition p470

560.q: ECV is absolutely contraindicated in all except:
560.e: Absolute Contraindications for ECV: Placenta previa Uterine abnormalities (e.g., fibroids or structural anomalies) Contracted Pelvis, CPD Maternal medical conditions (e.g., severe hypertension, cardiac disease) Fetal distress or non-reassuring fetal heart rate patterns IUGR Multiple pregnancies Rupture of membranes, Oligohydramnios ECV is performed with caution and without force in patients with lower uterine scar. Its a relative contraindication Reference : Fernando Arias 4/e, p 374

560.q: Not true about red degeneration of myomas is:
o: Due to interference with blood supply
560.e: Let us see each option one by one. Red degeneration of fibroid commonly occurs during pregnancy. (Option “a” is correct) The pathogenesis of fibroid is obscure but the initial change appears to be one of subacute necrosis which is presumably due to an interference with its blood supply. Some say that arterial or venous thrombosis is the basis of this and the lesion is the result of infarction. (Option “c” is thus correct). Red degeneration should be managed conservatively with bed rest and analgesics to relieve the pain. (option “d” is thus correct) There is no need for surgical intervention. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed p 355.

560.q: A 24 years old female came with 2 years of infertility and sub mucosal fibroids. She was scheduled for a myomectomy. All of the following measures reduce bleeding during myomectomy except:
560.e: Measures to control blood loss during myomectomy Preoperative GnRH analogs Moderate degree of edelberg position to enhance venous return Timing the surgery in the immediate postmenstrual phase. Hypotensive anaesthesia (using sodium nitro pruside) Use of vasoconstrictive agents mainly vasopressin intraoperatively Use of victor Bonney’s myomectomy clamp around blood vessels and round ligament Use of tourniquets around blood vessels Uterine artery embolisation (UAE) Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 604.

561.q: A 19-year-old woman gives a history of sharp pain in the lower abdomen for 2 days every month approximately 2 weeks before the menses. The most probable etiology for her pain is:
561.e: A female giving a history of sharp pain in lower abdomen, every month, 2 weeks before the menstruation suggests mittelschmerz as the diagnosis. Mittelschmerz is synonymous to painful ovulation. Pain is associated with rupture of ovarian follicle at the time of ovulation Ref. Dutta Gynae 4th/ed p 172, 5th/ed p 178

Ans, D. Hysterectomy Hysterectomy is the treatment of choice. Local resection can be tried in younger women in whom it is localized. Medical treatment oPtions are NSAIDS & hormonal therapy, though not much effective GnRH, danazole, Mirena IUCD for menorrhagea & pain.

561.q: Cause of secondary dysmenorrhea in a young female are all except:
561.e: Causes of secondary dysmenorrhea: PID Endometriosis Adenomyosis IUCD Uterine fibroid Polyps Cervical stenosis Congenital malformation of uterus like bicornuate uterus Management : Treatment of the underlying cause. Reference: Berek & Novak's gynecology 16th ed, p580

562.q: Which of the following is recommended for a newborn born to a mother suffering from acute viral hepatitis B infection?
562.e: HBIG is indicated for newborn infants of HBsAg-positive mothers, with initiation of the vaccine series at the same time, both within 12 hours of birth (administered at different injection sites). Infection at birth is associated with clinically silent acute infection but a 90% chance of chronic infection , whereas infection in young adulthood in immunocompetent persons is typically associated with clinically apparent acute hepatitis but a risk of chronicity of only ~1% Tenofovir is indicated in the management of chronic hepatitis B infection Reference : Harrison's Principles of internal medicine 21st ed chap 341 pg. 2592

562.q: As regard the PCOS and hyperinsulinemia:
o: Hyperinsulinemia is observed in about 40% to 80% of women with PCOS
Hyperinsulinemia stimulates hepatic synthesis of SHBG
Metformin has many other health benefits
562.e: Insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinaemia is observed in about 40% of women with normal weight and 80% obese women with PCOS. Hyperinsulinemia results in decreased hepatic synthesis of SHBG and increased ovarian androgen biosynthesis. Metformin reduces weight, BMI fasting insulin levels, blood pressure and LDL cholesterol. Metformin does not cause hypoglycemia neither in normoglycaemic patients nor with diabetic individuals. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed p 461-2, 470

562.q: Which of the following findings are seen in PCOS
562.e: There is no doubt that PCOS causes oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea, due to anovulation i.e.option a and b are correct. Pathologically - Ovaries are enlarged (2-5 times the normal size). Tunica albuginea is thickened. There is Theca cell hypertrophy (stromal hyperthecosis) and multiple follicular cysts are localized along the surface of the ovary (i.e.options 'c' is correct). Sonographic findings in case of PCOS include : ROTTERDAM CRITERIA >12 small cysts (2 to 9 mm in diameter) Increased ovarian volume (> 10 ml). Increased amount of stroma relative to the number of follicles. Only one ovary with these findings is sufficient to define PCOS. Other findings like Pearl necklace appear in which follicles are distributed underneath the capsule in a row. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed, pg 369-371

563.q: The progesterone component of OCP acts by:
o: Bringing about alterations in cervical mucus
563.e: Actions of the progesterone component of combined oral contraceptives: Suppresses ovulation by its inhibitory action on the pituitary and the hypothalamus. This is predominantly achieved by estrogens but even by progesterone. Causes atrophic changes in the endometrium and prevents nidation even if fertilization occurs. Acts on the cervical mucus, making it thick and tenacious and impenetrable by sperms. The third-generation progestogens have a higher affinity for progesterone receptor and have a role in inhibiting ovulation. The main function of progestogens in combined pills is to counteract the undesirable effects of estrogen such as endometrial hyperplasia and heavy withdrawal bleeding. Reference: SK Chaudhary 7 th /ed pp 125-126, 14.

563.q: Maximum success after reversal of tubal ligation?
563.e: Ans, C. Clip method The Falope sialistic ring destroys 2-3 cm fallopian tube. The Hulka& Filshie clips destroya smaller segment (3-4mm)' thus preserving the potential of successful reversal of surgery. The failure rate varies between .2 and 15%"

563.q: Oral contraceptive pills decrease incidence of all of the following conditions except:
563.e: Cancers/cysts Uterine cancer Ovarian cancers Fibroid uterus (Progesterone only pills) Ovarian cysts Benign breast diseases Benign disease of genital tract Endometriosis (if used continuously) PID (here Salpingitis) Ectopic pregnancy (as it decreases incidence of PID) They decrease ovulation thus, are helpful in Dysmenorrhea, premenstrual tension and Mittelschmerz syndrome. By decreasing blood loss they are helpful in menorrhagia and polymenorrhea. Acne and hirsutism (especially those containing desogestrel) OCPs are also beneficial in: DUB Hormone therapy for hypothalamic amenorrhea Prevention of menstrual porphyria. Reference: Shaw 15 th /ed pp 231-232; Dutta Obs 6 th /ed p 545; Harrison 17 th /ed p 563

o: It does not increase the risk of HIV
Treatment of male partners reduces recurrence.
Pregnant women should be routinely screened for bacterial vaginosis.
Atopobium vagina is associated with recurrence.
564.e: Associated with increased risk of acquiring HIV, C. trachomatis, and N. gonorrhoeae. Treatment of male partners with metronidazole does not prevent recurrence of bacterial vaginosis. Recurrence: Metronidazole gel twice weekly for >3 months Recommendation is against routine screening of pregnant women for bacterial vaginosis. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21 st ed, Ch: 136, Pg: 1083

564.q: A 46-year-old female suffering from severe menorrhagia underwent hysterectomy 6 years back. She wishes to take hormone replacement therapy. I/V/O hot flushes and atrophic vaginitis.The treatment of choice is:
564.e: Both estrogen alone or estrogen + progesterone can be used for treating menopausal symptoms. The choice depends on whether the uterus is present or not. "For women with a uterus, a progestin should be combined with an estrogen, to lower the risk of endometrial cancer." All women who have intact uterus should receive combined estrogen - progesterone therapy. Reference: Williams Gynae 1st/ed pp 495, 499-500

564.q: A young lady presents to your office with a complaint of copious vaginal discharge, but there is no cervical discharge on per speculum examination. Which of the following should be given for the management?
564.e: Syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections (WHO 1991) Principle: Treatment of STDs should be initiated at the patient's first visit to a clinic. At the same time the couple is counseled about the importance of condom use and prevention of STD transmission. Syndromic managements are based on epidemiological studies all over the world. Syndromic diagnosis and laboratory assisted diagnosis have been found similar in terms of accuracy. Method: Management is done by criteria for syndromic diagnosis of PID. These include detection of vaginal discharge abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, bilateral adnexal providers are trained up to follow a standardized protocol (flow chart) to treat such a patient. This is particularly suitable in a health care setting of developing countries. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed p 176; Internet search-www. naconlinr.org/upload/publication/ste

566.q: A 16-year-old boy is being treated with desmopressin for diabetes insipidus. His plasma glucose level (fasting) is 108 mg/dl, sodium 139 mmol/l (137-144), potassium 4.5 mmol/l (3.5-4.9) and calcium 10.9 mg/dl. He still has complaints of polyuria, polydipsia and nocturia. What could be the most probable cause?
566.e: This boy most probably has nephrogenic diabetes insipidus due to hypercalcemia. In this condition, renal tubules are resistant to antidiuretic hormone (ADH), which is due to a receptor defect of vasopressin-2 receptor or a post-receptor defect in an ADH-sensitive water channel called aquaporin-2. Central DI (ADH deficiency) show good response to desmopressin (V2 agonist) administration. The findings do not suggest diabetes mellitus, which is also associated with these symptoms. In patients with the syndrome of inappropriate secretion of ADH (SIADH), low sodium levels are the hallmark. Metabolic causes of Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: Chronic Hypokalemia Chronic Hypercalcemia Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 2920

566.q: Kalindi 25 years female admitted as a case of septic abortion with tricuspid valve endocarditis. Vegetation from the valve likely to affect is:
566.e: "Right sided endocarditis which usually involves the tricuspid valve causes septic pulmonary emboli occasionally with infarction and lung abscesses." Reference: CMDT '07, p 1447

566.q: The preferred site for obtaining cultures in a patient with acute PID during laparotomy is,
566.e: For identification of organisms in PID the materials are collected from the following available sources: Discharge from urethra or Bartholin’s gland Cervical canal Collected pus from the fallopian tubes during laparoscopy or laparotomy. The material collected is subjected to Gram’s stain and culture (aerobic/anaerobic). The findings of Gram-negative diplococci is suggestive of gonococcal infection. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed pg 130

567.q: Most common malignancy of fallopian tube
Which of the following pelvic structures is not developed from urogenital sinus?
567.e: The cloaca (endodermal) is divided by formation of the urorectal septum by the seventh week (7 th ) and is separated to create the rectum and the urogenital sinus. Urogenital sinus has 3 parts The cephalad or vesicle portion → urinary bladder The middle or pelvic portion → female urethra The caudal or phallic part → distal 1/3 of vagina (sinovaginal bulb) and the greater vestibular (Bartholin), urethral, and paraurethral (Skene) glands Reference : William's Obstetrics 25th Edition, chapter 7, page no. 121

567.q: Which one of the following congenital malformations of the fetus can be diagnosed in the first trimester by ultrasound?
567.e: As discussed in chapter on fetal malformation, anencephaly can be diagnosed as early as 8-10 weeks/first trimester in experienced hands. Microcephaly: - USG in Obs and Gynae Callen 4/e, p 298, 299 It has decreased head size. In these patients both brain mass and total cell number are reduced. There is a disproportion in size between the skull and face. It is difficult to recognize this anomaly by ultrasound - A head circumference below 2 SD from the mean is used as a diagnostic criteria in midtrimester scan. Holoprosencephaly is the presence of a single centrally placed cerebral ventricle and may be associated with midline abnormalities of the face. With the use of a vaginal probe it can be recognised in the beginning of midtrimester. Reference: Williams Obs. 21/e, p 1120; USG in Obs. and Gynae by Callen 4/e, p 284, Fernando Arias 3/e, p 64, 66, 69

568.q: A 44-year-old female complains of lower abdominal pain and vaginal discharge. On examination, there is cervicitis along with a mucopurulent cervical discharge. The Gram smear of the discharge shows presence of abundant pus cells, but no bacteria. The best approach to isolate the possible causative agent would be:
o: Culture on chocolate agar supplemented with hemin
Culture on a bilayer human blood agar
568.e: Patient is complaining of abdominal pain and vaginal discharge. On examination, cervicitis and mucopurulent discharge is seen - which indicates she is having PID. The presence of pus cells in the absence of an organism indicates chlamydial infection (most common STD today). It is an intracellular organism that grows only on McCoy or HeLa cell cultures. It cannot be grown on other media and hence, often goes unnoticed, later leading to infertility. Culture in McCoy cells is 100% specific for chlamydia but is inexpensive, technically difficult and takes 3-7 days to obtain the result. Reference: Harrion 18th/ed p 1426.

568.q: In the perspective of the busy life schedule in the modern society, the accepted minimum period of sexual cohabitation resulting in no offspring for a couple to be declared infertile is:
568.e: If a couple fails to achieve pregnancy after one year of “unprotected” and regular intercourse, it is an indication to investigate the couple for infertility. Infertility: Primary When no previous pregnancies have occurred. Secondary When a prior pregnancy although not necessary although not necessarily a live birth, has occurred Reference : Shaw 15 th /ed, p 200 Reference : Novak 13 th /ed, p 973

568.q: Most commonly used ovulation induction drug is
568.e: M/C used drug for ovulation Induction: clomiphene citrate Clomiphene Citrate: It is a racemic mixture of enclomiphene and zuclomiphene. Enclomiphene is a more potent isomer responsible for its ovulation-inducing action. Dose = 50–250 mg. However, the US FDA-approved maximum dose for clomiphene citrate is 100 mg Clomiphene blocks “Estrogen” receptors → increase FSH from pituitary →growth of follicles Thus it can be used only in patients with intact hypothalamic –pituitary ovarian axis With clomiphene success rate for ovulation is 80% and success rate for pregnancy is 40% Reference: JB Sharma textbook of Gynecology e1 p218

569.q: Chronic constipation in children is seen in all A/E?
569.e: Ans. is 'b' i.e., Jejunal polyp Organic causes of constipation are : i) Intestinal: Hirschprung disease, Anal/rectal stenosis, Anal fissure, anteriorly displaced anal opening, strictures. ii) Drugs: Narcotics, vincristine, Psychotropics. iii) Metabolic/endocrine: Cystic fibrosis, hypothyroidism, Panhypopituitrism iv) Neuromuscular: Cerebral palsy, Psychomotor retardation, spinal cord lesions, Myotonic dystophy, Neuropathy or myopathy of GIT v) Other causes: Low fibre diet, Milk protein allergy.

569.q: Which of the following statements is not true about cervical glands discharge
o: Cervical gland discharge is alkaline in nature and rich in mucoprotein
Vagina has no glands and acidic discharge of cervical glands makes vaginal ph low
Cervical gland secretions contain sodium chloride
None of the above (all are true)
569.e: Secretion of the cervical glands is alkaline and thick, rich in mucoprotein, fructose and sodium chloride. The vaginal pH , from puberty to menopause, is acidic because of the presence of Döderlein’s bacilli which produce lactic acid from the glycogen present in the exfoliated cells. The pH varies with the estrogenic activity and ranges between 4 and 5. Reference : DC Dutta textbook of obstetrics, 8th edition; chapter 1

569.q: Metropathica hemorrhagica is best treated by:
569.e: Metropathia hemorrhagica is a type of anovulatory DUB, hence logically speaking it should be best treated by progesterone therapy. It is mostly seen in premenopausal women. Patients complain of a variable period of amenorrhea followed by excessive painless bleeding. On HPE-cystic glandular hyperplasia, Swiss cheese pattern is seen, and secretory changes are absent Treatment: In DUB due to anovular causes: Progesterones are the mainstay of therapy. They diminish the effects of estrogen on target cells by inhibiting oestrogen receptors. Reference: Dutta Gynae 5 th /ed pp 184,187.

570.q: All of these secrete hormone, except:
570.e: Dysgerminoma: "The tumor is neutral and does not secrete either male or female sex hormones but secretes placental alkaline phosphatase, lactate dehydrogenase and beta hCG". Granulosa cell tumor : Secretes estrogen Theca cell tumor : Secretes estrogen Hilus cell tumor : Secretes androgens Reference: Shaw 15 th /ed p 378

570.q: The most common pure germ cell tumour of the ovary:
570.e: Germ cell Tumors of ovary: In contrast to slow growing epithelial ovarian tumors, germ cell malignancies grow rapidly and are characterized by subacute pelvic pain. Most common germ cell Tumor – Mature teratoma or Dermoid cyst (Benign in nature). Most common malignant GCT – Dysgerminoma. Second most common malignant GCT –Immature cystic teratoma Reference: CGDT 10 th/ed p 875; Devita 7th/ed p 1391; Novak 14th/ed p 1506; 15th/ed p 1394; Williams Gynae 1st/ed p 741

570.q: False about dermoid cyst of ovary:
570.e: Dermoid cyst: Dermoid cyst is a benign teratoma. It is most common benign tumour of ovary in reproductive age group. Most common benign neoplasm diagnosed during pregnancy. Most common Germ cell tumor. It is the commonest tumor to undergo torsion. Characteristically they are unilocular cyst containing hair and cheesy sebaceous material, teeth, bones, thyroid tissue and cartilage. If teeth or bone are seen in X-ray in adnexal mass, this finding is pathognomic for teratoma and thus X-ray is diagnostic. Malignant change in a dermoid cyst occurs in 0.5 – 2% cases in patients > 40 years. Most common malignancy which develops is, squamous cell carcinoma. Reference: Textbook of Gynaecology Sheila Balakrishnan 1 st /ed p 183 Reference: Shaw 15 th /ed p 376-7; Williams Gynae 1 st /ed p 214-5

571.q: What is the age group distribution for vulval cancer
571.e: Vulval Cancer Vulval cancer accounts for 2%-4% of all malignancies of the female genital tract. The women are generally elderly, in the sixth or seventh decade of life. Thirty per cent of cases are older than 70 years, and 40% of cases are between the age of 60 and 70 years. M/C variety- Squamous cell carcinoma Most common symptom of vulval cancer - pruritis Most common site: Labia majora and minora Most common type of spread: Lymphatics( First lympnode involved-Superficial Inguinal lymphnode, and then Deep inguinal LN and femoral group of lymphnodes). For lateral tumors only ipsilateral lympnodes involved whereas for midline leisons, B/L lymphnodes are involved Sentinel lymphnode biopsy is helpful in vulval cancer Most important prognostic factor- Lymph node status.

571.q: A 38-year-old woman approaches a physician for contraceptive advice. On examination, there were two symmetrical ulcers on her vulva, which were well-defined with a firm base. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
571.e: Painless well-defined ulcers with a firm base should raise the suspicion of a chancre. Chancre is the primary lesion of primary syphilis. It is most commonly found on the labium majus, labium minus, fourchette, clitoris, urethral orifice, or cervix, but can be found anywhere on the lower genital tract. In 10% cases, more than one primary lesion is present. The first manifestation is a small papule which breaks to form an ulcer. Ulcer is firm, painless with raised edges and a granulomatous base. In fact, any sort of discrete, relatively painless ulceration on the vulva may be a primary syphilitic lesion. Inguinal glands enlarge when the primary is on the vulva or lower vagina. Lymph nodes are hard, painless, and do not suppurate. Reference: Williams Gynaecology, 1st Edition, Page Number-58.

571.q: A lady approaches a physician for contraceptive advice. On examination, there were two symmetrical ulcers on the vulva, which were well-defined with a firm base. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
571.e: Chancre is the primary lesion of primary syphilis. It is most commonly found on the labium majus, labium minus, fourchette, clitoris, urethral orifice or cervix but can be found anywhere on the lower genital tract. In 10% cases more than one primary lesion is present. The first manifestation is a small papule which breaks to form an ulcer. Ulcer is firm, painless with raised edges and granulomatous base. In fact any sort of discrete relatively painless ulceration on the vulva may be primary syphilitic lesion. Inguinal glands enlarge when the primary is on the vulva or lower vagina. Lymph nodes are hard, short, painless, and do not suppurate. Reference: Harrison 17th/ed p 1040; William’s Gynae 1st/ed p 58-9 Current diagnosis and treatment of STDs p 21

572.q: Pap smear of janki, 46 years female shows CIN grade III. Which of the following is the next step in management?
572.e: Pap smear is only a screening test. To confirm we need to do a biopsy. In all visible lesions punch biopsy should be done In the case of invisible lesions, colposcopic directed biopsy is the gold standard. Thus, in this case since it is not mentioned growth is visible so we do colposcopy guided biopsy. Reference: Williams Gynecology 1 st /ed pg 628, Table 29-6

572.q: A 56-year-old female patient has carcinoma ovary with bilateral involvement with ascitic fluid in the abdomen. The stage is:
572.e: Bilateral involvement and malignant ascites is seen in category IC. In IC also- according to the new classification it is IC 3. Superficial liver metastasis is included in Stage III. Metastasis to liver parenchyma is included in Stage IV. Reference : Novak 14 th /ed pg 1477; Shaw 15 th /ed pg 427

572.q: A 42-year-old female P3 + 0 + 0 + 3 is found to have carcinoma in situ. Best treatment would be:
572.e: "Carcinoma in situ (stage 0) can be managed successfully by cone biopsy or by abdominal hysterectomy." Reference : Harrison 17 th /ed pg 608 Friends, carcinoma in situ is managed in young women with cone biopsy, whereas in older women or females who had completed their families (> 40 years), simple hysterectomy is the TOC. Reference : Harrison 17 th /ed pg 608; Reference : Novak 14 th /ed pg 581; Reference : Jeffcoate 6 th /ed pg 398

573.q: Which of the following investigations should be conducted in a 7-month-old child who has a hemoglobin level of 6.3, a history of recurrent blood transfusions, an MCV of 70 fl, normal MCH, normal MCHC, and a peripheral smear indicating a hypochromic microcytic image?
573.e: Explanation: In an infant with severe microcytic hypochromic anemia requiring transfusions, the most likely diagnosis is beta-thalassemia major . Hemoglobin electrophoresis is the definitive test, which would show a significant increase in Hemoglobin F (HbF) and possibly Hemoglobin A2 (HbA2) , with absent or reduced Hemoglobin A (HbA). Explanation of other options: Serum iron (Option A): Would be normal or elevated in thalassemia (due to transfusions), but low in iron deficiency. It is not the definitive test. Direct coomb's test (Option B): Used to diagnose autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Osmotic fragility test (Option C): Used to diagnose hereditary spherocytosis, which causes a normocytic or macrocytic anemia, not microcytic. Key Takeaways: Thalassemia major presents in infancy with severe transfusion-dependent microcytic anemia. Hemoglobin electrophoresis is the key diagnostic test.

Metropathia hemorrhagica is the same as cystic glandular hyperplasia and is a causative factor for endometrial cancer. Gynandroblastoma is a virilising tumor which secretes androgens (not estrogens) and so does not lead to endometrial cancer Dysgerminoma is a neutral tumor which doesnot secrete either male or female sex hormones but secretes placental alkaline phosphatase, LDH and BHCG and therefore doesnot lead to endometrial cancer. Reference : Shaw 14 th /ed pg 3386 Reference : Dutta Gynae 5 th /ed pg 184

573.q: Pain of ovarian carcinoma is referred to:
573.e: Ovarian pain is referred along the medial side of thigh The obturator nerve during its course, when runs in front of the internal iliac vessels is separated from the normally situated ovary by only the parietal peritoneum lining the pelvic wall, thus pain from the ovary may be referred along the nerve to the skin on the medial side of thigh. Also know Simpson Pain - colicky pain in patients of Ca Endometrium. It is referred to the hypogastrium or to both iliac fossae. It is not severe and tends to appear at the same time each day lasting only 1–2 hours. Reference : Lasts Anatomy 10th/ed pg 302

574.q: Narrowest part of fallopian tube is:
574.e: Parts are: Interstitium (Intramural): 1.25 cm long and 1 mm diameter (narrowest part). It has no longitudinal muscles; only circular muscles are present and acts as anatomical sphincter. Isthmus: 2.5 cm long and 2 mm in diameter (second narrowest part); acts as physiologic sphincter. Ampulla: Widest and longest part (5 cm) and fertilization occurs here. Fimbriae/infundibulum: 1.25 cm long with a maximum diameter of 6 mm Total length = 4 inches or 10–12 cm. Reference: Chapter 1, page 8, JB Sharma textbook of Gynecology

574.q: Glands of littre are homologous to:
574.e: The glands of labia minora are homologous to the glands of littre (glandulas prepuciales) of the penile portion of the male urethra Skene's Tubules Skene's tubules are the paraurethral glands equivalent to prostrate in males. Both Bartholin's glands and Skene's tubules arise as downgrowths of urogenital sinus. Bartholin's Glands Bartholin's Glands are homologous to Cowper's gland/bulbourethral glands in males. They are 2 in number and of racemose type. Lie in the superficial perineal pouch embedded in the posterior part of vestibular bulb. Glands are oval in shape and are the size of a pea. They are impalpable unless enlarged. The acini is lined by a single layer of low columnar or cuboidal cells. Reference: Shaw, 15/e, page 8

574.q: Which kind of epithelium is present in vagina?
574.e: In adult females, vagina is lined by stratified squamous epithelium. In newborn females, it is lined by transitional epithelium. Squamous epithelium is resistant to gonococcal infection. Thus, gonococcal vaginitis cannot occur in young/adult females. Reference : J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1 st edition pg 327

575.q: What is the normal color of stool in the newborn after first week of life?
575.e: Meconium (first stool) is passed within 24 hours. After that meconium stools (black tarry)can be passed upto 3 days. On 4th-5th days transitional stools (greenish) are passed. After 5 days regular milk stools (golden yellow) are passed. Tags: Topic: MISCELLANEOUS Difficulty level: GOOD TO KNOW Reference: Ghai essential pediatrics, 9 th ed, pg no: 133

575.q: What is the venous hematocrit level at which you will diagnose polycythemia in a newborn?
575.e: Definition of polycythemia: a. Venous haematocrit of over 65%. b. Venous haematocrit of over 64% at 2 hours age. c. An umbilical venous or arterial haematocrit over 63% or more. The mean venous haematocrit of term infants is 53 in cord blood, 60 at 2 hours of age, 57 at 6 hours of age and 52 at 12-18 hours of age. As the haematocrit increases, there is increased viscosity and decreased blood flow. When haematocrit increases to more than 60% there is a fall in O2 transport. Definition of hyperviscosity: Viscosity greater than 14.6 centipose at a shear rate of 11.55 as measured by a viscometer. (normal is 1.4- 1.8 centipoise).

575.q: You have to IV cannulate a newborn. The following things are available: 1. 22 G Cannula 2. 26 G Cannula 3. Gloves 4. Normal Saline 5. 5 ml Syringe Which among the following you shall be using for cannulation in this newborn?
575.e: This question is a practical application-based question and very similar to an actual question asked recently. The correct answer is D. For IV cannulating a neonate, we need Gloves, Cannula, Normal saline (to flush) and a 2 ml syringe (not a 5 ml syringe) In neonates, 26G Cannula is used. Reference: The Harriet Lane Handbook 23 rd Edition

576.q: A 3-year-old child presented with trouble walking to paediatrician. He is diagnosed with DMD (Duchenne muscular dystrophy) by polymerase chain reaction. Genetic analysis shows that the patient's gene for the muscle protein dystrophin on X chromosome contains a mutation. Mutation is found in its promoter region. Which would be the most likely defective process in this child?
o: Post translational modification in dystrophin protein
Post transcriptional modification in dystrophin mRNA
576.e: Option A & Option B: Translation is synthesis of protein from mRNA. Mutation in promoter regions does not lead to any problem during translation or post translational modifications. A deficiency of dystrophin mRNA will result in a deficiency in the production of the dystrophin protein. Option C: Mutations in the promoter typically prevent formation of the RNA polymerase II transcription complex, resulting in a decrease in the initiation of mRNA synthesis during transcription. Option D: Post transcriptional modifications like capping, splicing and tailing defects are not a consequence of promoter mutations. Reference: Harper’s illustrated biochemistry 32 nd edition CH 36 PN 379

576.q: A 14 year old boy has fevers. He has had elbow , shoulder and hip and knee pains over the last few months. On examination, he has a temperature of 37.5°C and palpable hepatosplenomegaly. Investigations show a CRP of 30 and negative ANA. What is the likely diagnosis?
576.e: Any arthritis that occurs in individuals Oligoarticular Polyarticular Rheumatoid factor positive Polyarticular Rheumatoid factor negative Systemic onset Psoriatic arthritis and Enthesitis related arthritis. Systemic onset JIA. It is characterised by Fever Evanescent rash Hepatosplenomegaly Generalized Lymphadenopathy Serositis They are prone for developing a life-threatening complication called Macrophage Activation Syndrome. They will be negative for ANA and RA factor. There will be anemia, raised ESR and CRP with transaminase elevation. Ferritin may be elevated and coagulation screen may be abnormal. Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21 st ed, Ch:58, Pg: 394

576.q: The use of prostaglandin to keep the ductus arteriosus open is necessary in which of the following?
576.e: Ductus dependent congenital heart disease (require a patent ductus for maintaining pulmonary / systemic circulation) - Transposition of Great arteries - Tetralogy of Fallot - Tricuspid atresia (Ebstein anomaly) - Coarctation of aorta - Hypoplastic left heart syndrome - Pulmonary stenosis PGE1 is used to maintain an open ductus arteriosus in neonates with heart lesions that depend on it for survival. In Gerbode defect, there is a direct communication between right atrium and left ventricle. Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 2011-12

577.q: Treatment of simple febrile convulsion is based on
577.e: Answer- A. Control of fever Prompt reduction of temperature by hydrotherapy (sponging) and antipyretics (paracetamole, ibuprofen) is the most important measure. If seizures lasts for more than 5 minutes, diazepam (rectal or IV) is the anticonvulsant of choice. Phenobarbitone is an alternative

577.q: A baby is born at 43 w 4 d of gestational age. Which of the following morbidity is not to be anticipated in this baby?
577.e: Morbidities associated with post-term pregnancy include the presence of Meconium-stained amniotic fluid ( option a) Meconium aspiration Oligohydramnios Non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing in labor Low apgar scores, Birth injury ( option c) Fetal macrosomia (option d) Fetal weight loss Tags : Topic : HIGH RISK NEWBORN Difficulty level : MUST KNOW Reference : Cloherty and Stark's Manual of Neonatal care, SA ed., pg. 88

577.q: A 2-day old neonate in the neonatal ICU develops seizures. Which of the following would be the next best investigation for the child?
577.e: In such a situation, BEDSIDE CRANIAL USG is a very useful and informative investigation. Cranial Ultrasound (CUS) in neonates is safe and radiation free. Safety of sonography is well established in fetus and infants CUS can be easily performed at the bedside. Reliable for commonly occurring neonatal events like hemorrhage, cystic lesions, major malformations and fluid collections. CUS can be initiated even immediately after birth and hence suitable for screening. It can be repeated as often as possible without any adverse effects and hence helps in proper follow up of babies with neurological problems. CUS is a significantly cheaper modality of neuroimaging compared with other techniques Reference: AIIMS NICU Protocols, 3 rd Edition

578.q: Mouthing of objects tends to significantly reduce by what developmental age in a child?
578.e: According to OP Ghai 10 th Ed, at 6 months, as the ability to chew develops, the child can take a biscuit to his mouth and chew. At this age, he tends to mouth all objects offered to him. This is called mouthing of objects and can be a reason for inadvertent foreign body ingestion or aspiration. This tendency abates by around 1 year of age in most children. According to other texts and sources, mouthing reduces between 12-18 months. Reference: OP Ghai 10 th Edition, Page 31

578.q: A child with developmental delay, can ride a tricycle, can copy a circle, can say name, knows own sex, but cannot narrate a story. What is the developmental age?
578.e: Age of attaining milestones normally Riding a tricycle comes normally at 3 years of age Saying full name and gender also comes at 3 years of age Copying a circle comes at 3 years of age Narrating a story comes at 4 years of age. Now, in this question, the child is able to perform the milestones corresponding to 3 years, but unable to do milestones related to 4 years. Hence, the developmental age of the child should be 3 years. Reference: OP Ghai 10 th Edition, Tables 3.1, 3.2 and 3.4

578.q: A normal infant is able to sits leaning forward with hands, reaches for and grasps cube with one hand, transfers objects between hands, cannot wave bye-bye, cannot hold objects between finger and thumb. Most probable age is?
578.e: Let us evaluate the information given in the question. A normal infant can sit with own support from 6 months onwards, also called as Tripod position. Reaching for and grasping a cube with one hand, also called as Unidextrous grasp comes at 6 months of age Transferring objects hands to hands develops between 6 to 7 months of age. Waving bye-bye develops at 9 months Immature Pincer grasp comes by 9 months and mature one by 12 months. So, the child is able to do milestones of at or before 7 months of age, but not attained milestones related to 9 months and beyond. Hence the probable age of the child is 7 months. References: OP Ghai 10 th Edition, Tables 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4; Nelson textbook of pediatrics, 20 th edition, pg-69

579.q: A baby boy born at 30 weeks of gestation is brought to you at 8 months of chronological age with complaint of not able to roll from prone to supine. What is the best next step of management?
o: Send genetic studies to find congenital disease
Send chromosomal array to find trisomy
Send to development pediatrician and occupational therapist for early intervention
579.e: Corrected gestational age = Chronological age- Preterm age = 32 weeks - 10 weeks = 22 weeks = 5.5 months Hence, the corrected age of the child is 5.5 months and usual age for the prone to supine is 6 months. Hence, the parents are to be reassured that child is normal for age. Till 2 years of age, correction of gestational age has to be applied. Tags : Topic : NORMAL DEVELOPMENT & ASSESSMENT Difficulty : MUST KNOW PYQ : NEET PG 2023 Reference : Ghai's Essential pediatrics, 8 th ed., pg. 50

579.q: Tanya had her first birthday party recently. During her party she was able to commando crawl with ease, but could not walk. She picked up all the gems from her cake. She could speak 2 words with meaning. She waved goodbye to her guests. Which are of Tanya's development is delayed?
579.e: Commando crawl (gross motor), picking up gems from cake- pincer grasp (fine motor), speaking 2 meaningful words (language), waving good bye (personal-social); all are achieved latest by 12 months. Hence, she has achieved all her milestones needed for her age. MILESTONES AT 12 MONTHS GROSS MOTOR Stand without support Walk with support FINE MOTOR Mature pincer grasp (holding like a pen) PERSONAL SOCIAL Plays a simple ball game LANGUAGE 1-2 meaningful words Tags : Topic : NORMAL DEVELOPMENT & ASSESSMENT Difficulty : MUST KNOW PYQ : FMGE JUNE 2022; NEET PG 2021 Reference : Nelson textbook of pediatrics, 21 st ed., pg. 137

579.q: Which of the following is most suggestive for suspecting cerebral palsy in children?
o: Smiling for the first time at 8 weeks
579.e: Hand preference, or handedness, is the tendency to use one hand more naturally and efficiently than the other for fine motor tasks. This usually develops in early childhood, often becoming clear between the ages of 2 and 4 Hand preference or hand dominance before 12 months of age is a red flag sign and needs evaluation. All other development milestone mentioned are achieved at optimal age. KEY TAKEAWAYS: Identifying and supporting hand preference helps children develop motor skills effectively, which can aid in tasks like writing and drawing as they grow Tags: Topic: CEREBRAL PALSY Difficulty level: MAY KNOW PYQ: NEET PG 2021 Reference: Nelson textbook of pediatrics, 21 st ed., pg. 143

580.q: A neonate has not passed urine in the last 24 hours since birth. Next step in management is?
580.e: According to Cloherty & Stark, 90% neonates void urine within 24 hours and 99% do so by 48 hours. Neonates without any risk factor can pass urine anytime before 48 hours of life. Until then we need to observe and feed the child. If more than 48 hours have passed, the baby needs to be shifted to the ICU and evaluated for volume status & investigated. Reference: Cloherty and Starks manual of neonatal care, SA ed., pg. 128

580.q: Breastfeeding should be started within how much time after birth?
580.e: Points to remember regarding breastfeeding Breastfeeding should be started as soon as possible after birth. As per WHO, UNICEF it must be started within 1 hr of birth Exclusive BF till: 6 months of age. Then start complementary feed and continue to breastfeed till 18-24 months. Reference: OP Ghai 10 th Edition, Page 142

580.q: Indication to use prednisolone in Henoch-Schoenlein Purpura is?
580.e: Treatment for mild and self-limited HSP is supportive, with an emphasis on ensuring adequate hydration, nutrition, and analgesia. Corticosteroids are most often used to treat significant GI involvement or other life-threatening manifestations. Glucocorticoids such as oral prednisone (1-2 mg/kg/day), or in severe cases, intravenous (IV) methylprednisolone for 1-2 wk, followed by taper, reduce abdominal and joint pain but do not alter overall prognosis. Corticosteroids are not routinely recommended for prevention of complications such as nephritis. Corticosteroids may also be needed in any orchitis, CNS involvement and pulmonary hemorrhage Reference: Nelson 21 st Ed, Chapter 192, OP Ghai 10 th Ed, Page 661

581.q: While treating the child with severe acute malnutrition, which of the following factor is not one of the criteria for discharge of the child?
581.e: Discharge criteria for SAM child Child is alert and active , eating atleast 120-130 kcal/kg/day with consistent weight gain of atleast 5g/kg/day on exclusive oral feeding Child is receiving adequate micronutrients Child is free of infections Child has completed immunization appropriate for age The caretaker has been sensitized for home-based care . Tags : Topic : SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION Difficulty level : MUST KNOW PYQ : NEET PG 2021; FMGE JAN 2022; AIIMS JULY 2020; FMGE JUNE 2022 Reference : Ghai's essential pediatrics, 9 th ed., pg. 107

581.q: Hepatitis B subunit vaccine is derived from?
581.e: The current subunit Hepatitis B vaccine is derived from surface antigen, i.e., HBsAg. The vaccine is based upon DNA recombinant technology and uses Aluminium as an adjuvant. The hepatitis B vaccine is made by taking the part of the virus that makes surface protein ("surface protein gene") and putting it into yeast cells. The yeast cells then produce many copies of the protein that are subsequently used to make the vaccine. Reference: OP Ghai 10 th Edition, Page 198

581.q: A 6-year-old female child presented with non-blanchable, palpable petechial rash on lower limbs and buttocks, along with 3+ urinary protein and joint pains in knee and ankle. There was a preceding sore throat 2 weeks back, which was conservatively managed. What is the therapy of choice?
581.e: The child was having a trigger factor in the form of sore throat & 2 weeks later, she presented with non-blanchable, palpable petechial rash on dependent parts, renal and joint involvement. This translates to a diagnosis of Henoch-Schoenlein Purpura, HSP- Also known as IgA Vasculitis. Management of HSP is Conservative- More than 90% improve in about 4 weeks. Steroids, e.g., Prednisolone are indicated in severe GIT involvement Reference: OP Ghai 10 th Edition, Page 661

582.q: Deficiency of which of the following vitamins is associated with increased risk of thrombosis?
582.e: Deficiency in vitamin E is associated with an increased risk of thrombosis, particularly in neonates, due to its role in platelet aggregation. Vitamin K deficiency leads to hemorrhagic disorders , since vitamin K is essential in the production of coagulation factors II, VII, IX, X, and proteins C and S. Increased bruising can be seen in vitamin C deficiency due to an inability to synthesize collagen. Vitamins A is not associated with either an increased bleeding or thrombosis risk.
