713.e: According to Freud there are five stages of psychosexual development. The approximate age range of the stages is characterised by: Oral phase : 1 year of fixation on mouth and lips – relation to sucking, biting and mouthing. Anal phase : 1–3 years of fixation on anal cavity – relation to toilet training. Phallic phase : 3–5/6 years of fixation and sensitivity to genitals. The Oedipus complex occurs only in this stage. Latency phase : 5/6 years of puberty – sexual preoccupations of earlier years repressed. Genital phase : puberty/maturity – new demands and sexual desires. This was described by Freud and occurs during the phallic stage of psychosexual development . The Oedipus complex derives its name from a classical Greek tragedy about Oedipus Rex who killed his father. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 4, page no. 157

714.q: Fetal alcohol syndrome is a known preventable cause of intellectual disability. Which of the following is true about alcohol use in pregnant women?
o: Any amount of alcohol use is not recommended during pregnancy
Up to 3 standard drinks per day in pregnancy is not causative for fetal alcohol syndrome
More than 7 standard drinks per week in pregnancy can lead to fetal alcohol syndrome
Occasional use of alcohol during pregnancy is not harmful
714.e: The National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism defines at-risk alcohol use for healthy nonpregnant women as > 3 drinks per occasion or > 7 drinks per week and any amount of drinking for women who are pregnant or at risk of pregnancy. Reference: Alcohol Use in Pregnancy (nih.gov)

714.q: Deciding to take an antacid before indulging in a spicy meal to avoid gastric distress is an example of which form of learning?
714.e: Negative reinforcement refers to giving a stimulus or event , which when its cessation or termination is contingent on a response, increases the likelihood that the response will occur again . Avoidance learning is seen in negative reinforcement , where to avoid an adverse event, the stimuli is avoided. For example, to avoid gastric distress, antacid is taken before eating a spicy meal. Reference : Morgan and King's Introduction to Psychology, 7th edition, Chapter 4 Principles of Learning, Page number 149.

714.q: A 25-year-old male, who once got trapped in an elevator, has now started avoiding all small enclosed spaces like other elevators, closed rooms, bathrooms, etc. for the fear that something embarrassing might happen to him there. The principle of Pavlovian conditioning which explains this is known as:
714.e: A person or animal tends to generalize the conditioned response to other stimuli that are somewhat similar to the original conditioned stimuli. The greater the similarity , the greater the generalisation among conditioned stimuli. Hence, in the above case scenario, where the person is phobic to all small enclosed spaces, which are like his original conditioned stimuli of being trapped in an elevator , is suggestive of stimulus generalisation. Reference : Morgan and King's Introduction to Psychology, 7th edition, Chapter 4 Principles of Learning, Page number 146.

715.q: Which of the following is a technique used in treatment of tic disorders?
715.e: Habit reversal technique is used in management of tic disorders. It involves several components aimed at increasing tic awareness, developing competing responses to tics and building and sustaining motivation and compliance. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 31.8c, Tourette's disorder, Page number 1202.

715.q: A 35-year-old married woman with a history of depressive disorder presents in the outpatient department complaining of loss of libido. Which antidepressant medication would be the most suitable to prescribe to address this side effect?
715.e: Mirtazapine has a lower incidence of sexual side effects than most other antidepressants at 24%. SSRIs may indirectly decrease libido through a direct inhibition of sexual arousal and orgasm.(Option A) Tricyclic antidepressants may decrease libido indirectly through sedation. Venlafaxine can inhibit arousal and orgasm.(Option D) Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 993.

715.q: You get a call from the duty obstetrician about a 32-year-old woman who was 15 week's pregnant and her bipolar affective disorder was stabilized on lithium. Which of the following statements about use of lithium in pregnancy is correct?
o: Lithium is not excreted in breast milk.
Lithium use does not affect the fetus in the second trimester.
Serum lithium levels increase in the third trimester of pregnancy.
Serum lithium levels increase in the immediate postpartum period.
715.e: Lithium is excreted in breast milk , so it should be explained clearly to the mother about the effect of lithium in newborn babies.( OPTION A IS FALSE ) Lithium can affect the baby during the second and third trimesters. It can have toxic effects if serum lithium levels are very high and can also cause cardiac dysfunction, diabetes insipidus and hypothyroidism in the fetus.( OPTION B IS FALSE ) Lithium levels fall during the third trimester of pregnancy.( OPTION C IS FALSE) However, immediately after delivery, the serum concentration starts to rise , so lithium levels should be closely monitored.( CORRECT OPTION D) Lithium use is usually associated with Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 987.

716.q: A child with untreated ADHD is most likely to develop which of the following disorders during adolescence?
o: Separation from parents leading to depression
716.e: Explanation: Untreated Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in childhood is associated with an increased risk of developing Conduct Disorder during adolescence. Children with ADHD often display impulsivity, aggression, and difficulty following rules, which may escalate into more severe behavioural problems, including violating the rights of others and engaging in antisocial behaviour . Explanation for other options: Binge eating (Option A) is not typically associated with untreated ADHD, although some individuals with ADHD may engage in emotional eating. Selective mutism (Option B) is more commonly associated with anxiety disorders and is not directly linked to ADHD. Separation from parent leading to depression (Option C) is not a common progression from ADHD, though emotional difficulties can arise, especially in children with comorbid conditions

716.q: A 50-year-old homeless male veteran is brought to the emergency department by the police for disruptive behaviour. On mental status examination, he has an elevated affect, but also has psychomotor agitation and paranoia; he says he "feels fantastic" but is wary of answering any questions, quickly becoming irritated. On physical examination, the patient exhibits a moderately elevated blood pressure and pulse rate. He is most likely intoxicated with which of the following substances?
716.e: Cocaine(or other stimulants such as amphetamine) intoxication can present with Euphoria Irritability Anxiety Psychotic symptoms such as paranoia Elevated vital signs Conversely, intoxication with alcohol, barbiturates, benzodiazepines and opiates generally causes depression, somnolence and depressed vital signs(OPTIONS A, B, & C). Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 20.9, Stimulant-related disorders, Page no. 675.

716.q: In a delirious patient, disturbances in attention increase towards the evening time due to sensory deprivation. This is known as:
716.e: In delirious state, the patient becomes more disturbed, disoriented, hyper vigilant towards the evening after sunset due to sensory deprivation. This is known as sun downing. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Comprehensive Textbook of Psychiatry, 10 th edition, Chapter 10.2 Delirium, Page number 3062.

717.q: A 25 year old female is presented to OPD with complaints of agitation, muttering to herself and sleep disturbances. She claims that her husband has stolen the baby from her womb. She has delivered a healthy child three weeks back, however has not taking care of the baby. What is the most probable diagnosis?
717.e: Nihilistic delusion is associated postpartum and duration is around 3 weeks. Diagnosis is Postpartum psychosis. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 8, Page No.: 357

717.q: Which one of the following is NOT a poor prognostic factor in OCD?
717.e: It is observed that about 20–30% of those with OCD show a significant improvement, 40–50% have a moderate improvement, while the rest have a chronic or worsening course. Poor prognostic factors include yielding to compulsions, a childhood onset , male , bizarre content of compulsions, need for hospitalization , a coexisting major depressive disorder , the presence of overvalued ideas , and the presence of personality disorder (especially schizotypal). (Option A, B & C) A good prognosis is indicated by good premorbid adjustment, the presence of a precipitating event, and episodic nature. The content or theme of obsessions and family history do not relate to the prognosis . Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 10, page no. 420

717.q: Which of the following is/are leading cause of death among 15-24 years old?
717.e: Unintentional injury and homicide were the leading causes of death among residents ages 15-24, each accounting for 34.2% and 32.9%, respectively, of all deaths. These were followed by suicide (9.9%) and cancer (5.8%). Accidents (unintentional injuries), homicide, suicide, cancer, and heart disease make up the five leading causes of death for teenagers Reference : https://cchealth.org/health-data/hospital-council/2010/pdf/11_lcd_by_age.pdf

718.q: A 12-year-old girl complains of feeling depressed frequently and having nightmares since last 4 months. On delving deeper, she revealed to the psychiatrist that she has been having these symptoms after one of her uncles molested her in an isolated place. She has not talked about this event to anyone (including her parents) due to shame and requests the psychiatrist too not to reveal it to anyone. What should be the role of psychiatrist in this case?
o: Confidentiality in this case can't be breached as the patient has denied revealing
Confidentiality should be breached as this is a matter of child sexual abuse
Confidentiality can be breached only after taking consent of the patient in this case
Confidentiality should only be breached if the matter involves legal court
718.e: If a child has been the victim of physical or sexual abuse, then psychiatrists are required to make an immediate report to an appropriate agency . ( Option B is CORRECT ) In this situation, confidentiality is decisively limited by legal statute on the grounds that potential or actual harm to vulnerable children outweighs the value of confidentiality in a psychiatric setting. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 36.1 Forensic Psychiatry, Page number 1383.

718.q: Which statements are correct with respect to Mental Healthcare Act 2017 ? 1. Suicidal act has been decriminalised 2. 720.q: Which of the following is the most important feature in determining the malignancy of cystic ovarian lesion?

721.e: Ionizing radiation is the term given to forms of radiation that are energetic enough to displace orbiting electrons from the atoms in the absorbing medium, thus forming positive ions. High Energy Electromagnetic Radiation like X Rays, Gamma Rays, and Cosmic Rays are Ionising Radiation Particulate Radiation Like Alpha, Beta, Protons, Neutrons, and Electrons are Ionising Radiation. Most other electromagnetic radiation like UV rays, Visible light, Infrared Rays, Radiowaves are Nonionising Sound waves used in Ultrasound are also Nonionising. Reference: Bell, D. Ionizing radiation. Reference article, Radiopaedia.org. https://doi.org/10.53347/rID-59177

722.q: Gastric emptying studies using radionuclides are used in?
722.e: Gastric emptying studies (GES) using radionuclides are performed to evaluate gastric motor function. They are often considered the "gold standard", and "most physiologic" examinations, because of their noninvasive nature, use a physiologic liquid or solid meal, and the resultant quantitative information. Typical indications for GES are evaluation of symptoms such as (postprandial) nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain, gastroesophageal reflux disease, difficult glycemic control in diabetic patients, suspected or known gastroparesis, and assessing response to therapy. 723.q: On which of the following modalities is junctional zone of endometrium best visualised
723.e: MRI was the first imaging technique to permit the visualization of the uterine junctional zone and remains the imaging method of choice to evaluate it and its associated pathology. Junctional zone is a region representing the inner myometrium and is a very important imaging feature in pelvic MR imaging for interpretation of various pathologies. 724.q: MRI is based on the principles of ?

725.q: Which of the following type of mucor mycosis is commonly seen in COVID 19 pneumonia
725.e: Mucor mycosis can involve nose, sinuses, orbit, central nervous system (CNS), lung (pulmonary), gastrointestinal tract (GIT), skin, jaw bones, joints, heart, kidney, and mediastinum (invasive type), but ROCM is the commonest variety. It should be noted that term ROCM refers to the entire spectrum ranging from limited sino nasal disease (sino-nasal tissue invasion), limited rhino-orbital disease (progression to orbits) to rhino-orbital-cerebral disease (CNS involvement). The area of involvement may differ due to underlying condition. Reference: Singh, Awadhesh Kumar et al. “Mucor mycosis in COVID-19: A systematic review of cases reported worldwide and in India.” Diabetes & metabolic syndrome vol. 15,4 (2021): 102146. doi:10.1016/j.dsx.2021.05.019

725.q: A 2 year old child presents with a sudden onset of breathing difficulty while playing. CXR shows unilateral lucent hemithorax with normal left lung. Which of the following statement is true in this condition?

Focal area of decrease air entry confirms the diagnosis
In complete obstruction, ball valve mechanism to such condition
Prefer way of removing is rigid bronchoscopy
725.e: Unilateral hemithorax in a child with sudden breathing difficulty suggests foreign body in lungs. It is removed by rigid bronchoscope, not partial. Focal areas of reduced air entry can also occur in collapse; it doesn't confirm the diagnosis. Ball valve mechanism occurs in partial obstruction not complete.

725.q: All are features of Kerley A lines except?
o: Due to lymphatic engorgement and edema of septa
725.e: Kerley A lines are Perihilar Lines Kerley B lines are thin horizontal parallel lines perpendicular to pleura at base of Lung Kerley lines on a chest X-ray are thin linear opacities that can be associated with congestive heart failure (CHF). They are often classified into three types: Interstitial Kerley B Lines: Appear as short, horizontal lines at the lung periphery. Indicate interstitial edema, common in CHF. Septal Lines (Kerley A Lines) Vertical lines extending from the hila to the periphery. Result from fluid accumulation in the interlobular septa. Peribronchial Cuffing (Kerley A Lines): Short lines near the hila, representing fluid around bronchi. Suggestive of peribronchial edema. In CHF: X-ray findings often include cardiomegaly (enlarged heart). Increased vascular markings due to fluid retention. Pleural effusions may be present.

726.q: Which of the following is seen on CXR in COVID 19 patients?
726.e: Findings of COVID-19 on chest radiographs vary, ranging from normal in the early stages of disease to unilateral or bilateral lung opacities, sometimes with a basilar and strikingly peripheral distribution. Early research reported a relatively low sensitivity (69%) for the diagnosis of COVID-19 using baseline chest radiography. Although underlying comorbidities such as chronic lung disease or congestive heart failure may confound chest radiograph interpretation, studies have shown that many of the hallmark chest CT findings are apparent on chest radiograph Reference: COVID-19 Imaging: What We Know Now and What Remains Unknown Jeffrey P. Kanne, Harrison Bai, Adam Bernheim, Michael Chung, Linda B. Haramati, David F. Kallmes, Brent P. Little, Geoffrey Rubin, and Nicola Sverzellati Radiology 2021 299:3, E262-E279

727.q: Which of the following artery is used in management of fetal anemia?
727.e: Fetal Doppler US of the middle cerebral artery is used in two situations: (a) noninvasive assessment of fetal anemia and (b) calculation of cerebroplacental ratio as a measure of fetal brain sparing. In response to hypoxia, the fetus diverts blood flow to the brain, increasing the middle cerebral artery diastolic flow, thereby decreasing the pulsatility index and altering the ratio of the umbilical artery flow to the middle cerebral artery flow. Reference: A Radiologist’s Guide to the Performance and Interpretation of Obstetric Doppler US Anne M. Kennedy and Paula J. Woodward RadioGraphics 2019 39:3, 893-910

728.q: Drop Metastasis due to CSF spread is seen with all except?
728.e: Drop metastasis refers to the spread of tumor cells through the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leading to seeding of the leptomeninges along the spinal cord or brain surface. This phenomenon is seen in certain types of brain tumors, particularly those originating in or near the ventricles or meninges. Medulloblastoma (A), Pineal germinoma (B), and Ependymoblastoma (C) are all types of brain tumors that can spread through the CSF and cause drop metastasis. Oligodendroglioma (D), however, typically does not exhibit this pattern of spread. Oligodendrogliomas are more likely to spread locally within the brain rather than through the CSF.

729.q: Some of the other contrast agents used in MRI are ___ and ___
729.e: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agents are either paramagnetic ion complexes or superparamagnetic magnetite particles and contain lanthanide elements such as gadolinium (Gd3+) or transition metal manganese (Mn2+). These elements shorten the T1 or T2 relaxation time, thereby causing increased signal intensity on T1-weighted images or reduced signal intensity on T2-weighted images. Most paramagnetic contrast agents are positive agents. These agents shorten the T1, so the enhanced parts appear bright on T1-weighted images. Dysprosium, superparamagnetic agents and ferromagnetic agents are negative contrast agents. The enhanced parts appear darker on T2-weighted images. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 772

729.q: Gadolinium based contrast agents for MRI can be safely given in lactating mothers.
729.e: Gadolinium based contrast agents for MRI can be safely given in lactating mothers as very little is excreted in milk and absorbed from the gut. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 772

730.q: After consuming a black buck after hunting it down, a patient develops headache, flushing, vomiting, blurry vision, and confusion. The consumption of which of the following should have been avoided to prevent this toxicity?
730.e: The clinical scenario is suggestive of vitamin A toxicity. Blackbuck's liver should not be consumed to avoid toxicity of vitamin A. Vitamin A and other fat-soluble vitamins are stored particularly in the liver and adipose tissue. Vitamins can be broadly classified into two categories fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and water-soluble vitamins (B, C) Reference: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page Number-527.

730.q: A 50-year-old male, who is a known case of PLHA, has had complaints of headache and dizziness for 2 days. Which of the following cells in the brain are predominantly infected by HIV?
730.e: The clinical syndrome of CNS abnormalities is called HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND). Microglia, cells in the CNS that belong to the macrophage lineage, are the predominant cell types in the brain that are infected with HIV. It is believed that HIV is carried into the brain by infected T cells or monocytes. The mechanism of HIV-induced damage of the brain remains obscure. Because neurons are not infected by HIV and the extent of neuropathologic changes is less than expected from the severity of neurologic symptoms, most workers believe that the neurologic deficit is caused indirectly by viral products and by soluble factors produced by infected microglia. Reference: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10 th Edition, Page Number-253.

730.q: A 45 year old female presents with recurrent headache, MRI reveals extraaxial, intradural and early enhancing lesion, All are Radiological features of this tumor except?
730.e: Calcification: True. Meningiomas can often exhibit calcifications, which can be seen on imaging. Vascular markings: True. Meningiomas can show prominent vascular markings due to their vascularity. Hyperostosis: True. Meningiomas can cause hyperostosis or thickening of adjacent bone due to their slow-growing nature and pressure effect on bone. Drop metastasis: False. Drop metastasis refers to the seeding of tumor cells along the spinal cord or brain surface via the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which is not a characteristic feature of meningiomas. It is more commonly associated with medulloblastomas and other tumors that spread through the CSF.

737.q: Remote after loading is used in:-

In principle, complete elimination of all unnecessary radiation exposure is possible by 'remote after-loading ,' which has been used for small teleradium bombs for more than twenty-five years and is widely applied in industrial radiography with gamma-ray sources. 739.q: Which of the following favours Aortitis?
739.e: Ascending aortic aneurysms can indeed occur in various conditions, including vasculitis and syphilis, but they can also be caused by other factors such as atherosclerosis, genetic conditions (e.g., Marfan syndrome), bicuspid aortic valve, or as a complication of cardiac surgery. These aneurysms involve the section of the aorta that rises from the heart and can be serious if they rupture. Early detection and management are crucial.

739.q: All the following can lead to an increase in temperature of the body in the first two hours following death except:
739.e: Cholera, septicemia, and sunstroke lead to an increase in body temperature in the first two hours following death. It is due to postmortem caloricity. Postmortem caloricity is the condition in which the temperature of the body remains raised for the first two hours or so after death. This occurs: When the regulation of heat production has been severely disturbed before death, as in sunstroke, pontine hemorrhage and in some nervous disorders. When there has been a great increase in heat production in the muscles due to convulsions, as in tetanus and strychnine poisoning, or increased muscular activity as in cases of violent asphyxial deaths (struggle prior to death) etc. When there has been excessive bacterial activity, as in septicemic conditions like cholera and other fevers. Reference: The Essentials of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology by KS Narayan Reddy, 35th Edition, Page Number-114.

739.q: A 30-year-old lady after undergoing miscarriage was found to be positive for the VDRL. Test for confirmation, gold standard investigation using fluorescent treponemal antibody test was done, which was found to be negative. Why was this discrepancy in the result observed?
739.e: Cardiolipin which is the phospholipid with antigenic properties is responsible for this discrepancy. VDRL contains cardiolipin -cholesterol - lecithin mixtures to detect serum antibodies formed against treponema pallidum. This lady who is undergoing further evaluation for her prior miscarriage probably has an anti-cardiolipin antibody. Here, serum that cross-reacts with the component of the VDRL reagent resulting in the biological false positive VDRL. However, the confirmatory test suggests that anti cardiolipin antibody is not due to infection with treponema pallidum but due to some other reason. Reference: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page Number-200.
